source: THE FULL-EPIC TRAILER (pipeline number 97; never a numbered episode). One image and at most one short line per beat, from Bhishma's vow to the last walk, then the word itihasa. EVERY beat was read in the constituted text of the BORI Critical Edition (GRETIL e-text, lab/ce/): the verses, a Sanskrit quotation for each, and everything cut or reworded are in script/TRAILER-CHECK.md. In short: 6.55.86-98 (the cold open: Krishna raises the wheel and runs at Bhishma; Arjuna holds him; the wheel is not thrown), 1.94.86-90, 1.104.10-15 and 3.292.6-7, 1.107.1, 1.132.8-12 and 1.136.4-10, 1.139.1-4 and 1.142.28-31, 1.155.41, 1.179.14-22 (five arrows), 2.42.21-25 (the wheel released: Shishupala), 2.53-54 and 2.58.29-37, 2.60.22-28, 2.61.40-41 (the cloth: no cause is named; Krishna's part is star passage 543* and is not shown), 2.67.9-10, 5.125.26, 6.23.21-47 and 6.24.9-11, 6.114.81-85, 7.33.12 and 7.48.9-14, 8.66.42-65 and 8.67.24, 10.8.5-12, 11.16.1-4 and 11.25.36-42, 17.1.23-31 and 17.3.7-8, 1.1.52 (itihasa). 'Iti-ha-asa: so indeed it was' is the traditional analysis of the word, not a verse.
structure: COLD OPEN (the most arresting image, the title as a statement) -> the story in order, one image a beat, cut fast -> REST 1 and the conch -> the war by its consequences -> REST 2, a full stop of all sound -> the word itihasa in its three parts, its meaning, the promise, the invitation.

names.Karna: born in armour, a charioteer's foster-son

strings.sourceLine: Text: the Mahabharata · BORI Critical Edition

lines.text: This is the Mahabharata. All of it.
lines.note: COLD OPEN (CE 6.55.86-98): Krishna, the wheel raised and blazing, down from the chariot and running at Bhishma; Arjuna has him by the arm. The title low in the frame from frame 1.

lines.text: A prince swears away his throne and his line.
lines.note: CE 1.94.86-90: the young prince, a hand raised, before the fisher-king on the river bank; flowers rain. Plaque: Bhishma.

lines.text: A mother gives her first-born to the river.
lines.note: CE 1.104.10-15, 3.292.6-7: a girl kneels at the water; a basket goes out on the river with a child in it, gold armour and earrings shining. Plaque: Karna.

lines.text: A hundred brothers. Five cousins. One throne.
lines.note: CE 1.107: Duryodhana large and grave in the foreground, the mace upright; beyond him, in focus second, five figures. Plaque: Duryodhana.

lines.text: A palace built to burn.
lines.note: CE 1.132, 1.136: the lacquered house goes up; a tilt down to six small figures leaving by a tunnel under it with one lamp.

lines.text: In the forest, Bhima breaks a man-eating demon.
lines.note: CE 1.139.1-4, 1.142.28-31: the rakshasa Hidimba, huge, ember-red, tawny-eyed, reaches; Bhima, as big, takes him by the arms. Plaque: Hidimba.

lines.text: A woman rises from a fire-altar.
lines.note: CE 1.155.41: Draupadi rises out of the middle of the fire-altar. Plaque: Draupadi.

lines.text: An archer brings down the mark and wins her.
lines.note: CE 1.179.14-22: Arjuna looses; the mark on its pole comes down (five arrows); a white garland. Plaque: Arjuna.

lines.text: Krishna lets the wheel fly.
lines.note: THE SIGNATURE SHOT (CE 2.42.21-25): Krishna, large; the wheel leaves his hand, a ring of fire across the frame; a light rises from where it went and comes back into him. Plaque: Krishna.

lines.text: Then the dice. A king stakes his kingdom, his brothers, his wife.
lines.note: CE 2.53-54, 2.58: Shakuni throws; from above the dice turn on the red cloth and the stakes slide away one after another. Plaque: Shakuni.

lines.text: She is dragged before the kings.
lines.note: CE 2.60.22-28: Draupadi, hair loose, a hand on her wrist pulling her across the frame past the pillars; the hall's seated heads.

lines.text: They pull at her cloth. The cloth does not end.
lines.note: CE 2.61.40-41: the cloth is pulled, and there is more cloth, and more: it runs out of frame in a long red band. No cause is shown. She stands; the heads in the hall are bowed.

lines.text: Thirteen years of exile.
lines.note: CE 2.67.9-10: six small figures walk away under great trees.

lines.text: Duryodhana will not give a needle-point of earth.
lines.note: THE CLOSE-UP (CE 5.125.26): Duryodhana's face, lamp-lit: resolve hardening; his eye goes to the one he is refusing. A king holding his ground.
THE TURN, unvoiced, after a real silence held on Duryodhana's face (CE 6.1.1-3, 6.23): the conch; two armies drawn up on the plain, banners, dust; one chariot comes out between them. A crane down.

lines.text: Two armies. Arjuna lowers his bow. Krishna speaks.
lines.note: CE 6.23.21-47, 6.24.9-11: the chariot between the armies; Arjuna sits and lets the bow fall; Krishna turns to him and speaks.

lines.text: Bhishma falls, and lies on a bed of arrows.
lines.note: CE 6.114.81-85: at sunset Bhishma lies on the arrows and does not touch the ground. A pull back.

lines.text: A boy fights alone, and many bring him down.
lines.note: CE 7.33.12, 7.48.13: Abhimanyu alone, sword up, inside a ring of spears and chariot wheels that closes. The blow is not shown. Plaque: Abhimanyu.

lines.text: Karna's wheel sinks into the earth.
lines.note: CE 8.66.60-65, 8.67.24: the chariot wheel sunk in the earth; Karna's hands on it, heaving; behind him the red sun going down.

lines.text: A night raid on a sleeping camp.
lines.note: CE 10.8.5-12: night; dark tents; one figure with a blade goes in, not by the gate.

lines.text: A mother of a hundred sons curses Krishna.
lines.note: CE 11.16.1-4, 11.25.36-42: Gandhari, blindfolded, a hand raised toward Krishna; behind them a field of fires to the horizon. Plaque: Gandhari.

lines.text: At the end, a king will not abandon his dog.
lines.note: CE 17.1.23-31, 17.3.7: snow and a mountain; one old king in bark cloth walking up; a dog at his heel; he stops and turns to it. Plaque: Yudhishthira.

lines.text: It calls itself itihasa.
lines.note: After a full stop of all sound (CE 1.1.52): dark; the word in gold, itihasa.

lines.text: Iti. Ha. Asa. So indeed it was.
lines.note: The word splits into its three parts as they are spoken, each with its gloss under it; then the meaning.

lines.text: All of it, start to finish. Nothing added for effect.
lines.note: The Naimisha fire at the blue hour; the storyteller comes to it.

lines.text: Follow. Episode one.
lines.note: First light: Vyasa, lit, large, a hand open to us, beside the great fire; the source line (fixed); Episode 1's title. The shot keeps drifting to the last frame.
